clue.text: Monkey with number plunged into wild stream

indicators.note: the number dives into the middle of the word for wild, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: wild means mad, as in furious
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A monkey carrying a number tag has been dropped into a raging brook.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrill is a large West African baboon-like primate with a brightly coloured face.

clue.text: Sellers for example talk at length

explanation.surface: Peter Sellers was known to ramble on.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers was one of the stars of The Goon Show, a classic BBC radio comedy, so he is an example of a Goon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sellers was a member of the radio comedy team, and to go on is to talk tediously and lengthily.

clue.text: Solar deity, male, above earth, ascending

parts.note: he is a male pronoun

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word for earth is read from bottom to top

parts.note: soil is earth

explanation.surface: A sun god, a man, rises above the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the sun was personified as a god who drove his chariot across the sky.

clue.text: Potato salad initially, then dessert

indicators.note: initially picks out only the opening letter of the word salad

parts.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A meal plan: potato salad to start, then pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: PUD is British informal for pudding, the sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is a common informal word for a potato.

clue.text: Lad involved with crime is making denial

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled up, so the letters of these words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A boy caught up in wrongdoing is denying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges LAD, CRIME and IS; 'with' and 'making' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclaimer is a formal statement renouncing responsibility, a kind of denial.

clue.text: Desire soldiers displayed for glory

parts.note: lust is strong desire
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops showed their appetite for military fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre can mean splendour or distinction, the brilliance of fame.

clue.text: Lexicographer, spoken about, succeeded in purpose

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for spoken is read backwards

parts.note: oral means spoken

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for purpose

parts.note: use is purpose, as in 'what's the use?'
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A dictionary-maker, much talked about, achieved his aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ORAL into LARO; 'spoken about' looks like a homophone signal but is not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Larousse was the nineteenth-century French compiler of the famous dictionaries bearing his name.

clue.text: Very fast comprehending mass, not at all dozy

indicators.note: comprehending means taking in, so the joined outer words wrap round the inner pieces

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
Lent is the Christian season of fasting
M is the physics symbol for mass
no can mean not at all, as in 'no better'

explanation.surface: Someone extremely quick, grasping a great deal, is anything but sleepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehending' takes in a two-part shell: the words for 'Very' and 'fast' join, and the mass symbol plus 'not at all' sit between them; 'fast' as a religious fast is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy, inclined to sleep.

clue.text: With financial obligation fulfilled, conceited youngster conceals relief

indicators.note: conceals means hides inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky or conceited young man
aid is relief, as in famine relief

explanation.surface: Debts settled, a cocky young man hides his sense of relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A paid-up member has settled all dues owed.

clue.text: Material obtained by digging around

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word for digging is read backwards

parts.note: mined means dug, describing excavation

explanation.surface: Fabric acquired by excavating the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns MINED backwards; 'digging' must be read as a past form, mined.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing twill cotton fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Show energy, following leader of army in charge

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the energy symbol is placed at the end
in places the letter inside the word for charge

parts.note: to indict is to charge formally with a crime

indicators.note: leader of takes just the opening letter of army

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energy on display, following the head of the army in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' looks like a phrase meaning commanding; it is 'in' as a container plus 'charge' as INDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or show.

clue.text: Futile pursuit in City lashed by old sage who is getting animated

indicators.note: lashed by means bound round, so the anagram is tied around the abbreviation
getting animated means stirred into motion, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: In the City, an old wise man gets whipped up and excited.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postcode is inserted midway through the rearranged letters; the 14-letter answer has no printed enumeration in this source.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild-goose chase is a hopeless quest for something unattainable.

clue.text: Protest, large one, over outhouse being knocked down

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
I is the Roman numeral one
a shed is an outhouse

explanation.surface: A big protest takes place above a shed that is being razed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places DEMO, L and I above SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolished means razed, pulled down.

clue.text: Approved comic, far out, you'll find entertaining shortly

annotationWithheld.why: 'Approved comic, far out, you'll find entertaining shortly' (OCR): CANONICAL looks like COMICAL with OM out and ANON (shortly) inside, but nothing printed gives OM; 'far' seems a misread no search confirms
annotationWithheld.clue: Approved comic, far out, you'll find entertaining shortly

clue.text: Move awkwardly in saddle

explanation.surface: Riding badly, the rider shifts clumsily on the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: To lumber someone, a British usage, is to saddle them with an unwanted burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbering is moving heavily and clumsily; to burden someone with a task is to lumber them with it.

clue.text: Style coming to be seen as sententious

indicators.note: to style is to arrange or fashion, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new fashion emerging is regarded as preachy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' reads as a noun but is the anagram signal, a verb meaning arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomic means expressed in short pithy maxims, as sententious writing is.

clue.text: Exclusive tavern's set up — jar can be had outside it

indicators.note: had outside it means the word for jar surrounds the reversed piece

parts.note: to jar is to clash, as colours do

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: an inn is a tavern; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A pub is opened with a jug of drink round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clannish means sticking within a close group and keeping outsiders out.

clue.text: One anxious about health inspector broaching 4 beer cask admitted to unfinished modification

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so the beer and cask go into the shortened word
unfinished drops the last letter of the word for modification

parts.note: a variant is a modified form
ale is beer

indicators.note: broaching means piercing a cask, so the inspector goes inside it

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A health worrier: a detective opens a barrel and is let into an incomplete change.
explanation.walkthrough: The '4' in the printed clue does nothing; it is most likely an OCR misreading of 'a'. 'unfinished' turns VARIANT into VARIAN, and the beer and pierced cask sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A valetudinarian is a hypochondriac, someone obsessively concerned with their own health.

clue.text: Room in tube for mice?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for tube

parts.note: a vein is a blood-carrying tube

explanation.surface: A space in a pipe for rodents to live in.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice are a typical example of pests, and the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Bad artist endlessly seen around northern river

indicators.note: seen around means placed about, so the shortened word surrounds the letter
endlessly removes the final letter

parts.note: a dauber is an unskilled painter

explanation.surface: A poor painter, unending, is spotted round a river in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major European river flowing to the Black Sea.

clue.text: Journalist, first in pyramid connected with leader of Egypt, holding mike, going backwards

indicators.note: first in takes just the opening letter of pyramid
holding means containing, so the reversed name wraps round the letter
going backwards means the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Gamal Abdel Nasser was president of Egypt
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A reporter at a pyramid with Egypt's ruler, carrying a microphone, retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of Egypt' looks like a first-letter pick (E) but is Nasser; 'going backwards' gives RESSAN, which holds M.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressman is a newspaper reporter, a member of the press.

clue.text: Dog, dirty, having head and tail scrubbed

indicators.note: head and tail scrubbed means the first and last letters are wiped away

parts.note: smutty means dirty, either grimy or obscene

explanation.surface: A grubby dog has its head and tail washed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutt is a mongrel dog.

clue.text: Fowl around little lake that lacks depth

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means around

indicators.note: lacks depth removes the D, the abbreviation for depth

parts.note: a pond is a small lake

explanation.surface: A bird circles a shallow pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table.

clue.text: Spun yarn? Here's the part of it that's weak

indicators.note: part of it says the answer is a run of letters lying within the preceding words

explanation.surface: Asking which bit of a spun thread is the flimsy part.
explanation.definitionFit: Puny means feeble or undersized.

clue.text: Urgent court order

parts.note: dire can mean urgent, as in dire need

explanation.surface: A pressing injunction issued by a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court order' looks like a single legal term, but only 'order' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct is to command or instruct.

clue.text: Doctor protecting lord with singular courage

indicators.note: protecting means shielding all round, so one word wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: Bones is slang for a doctor, famously the ship's doctor in Star Trek
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A physician shields a peer with a single act of bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Boldness is daring, bravery.
